metaDescription: Five 3 ton floor jacks compared by steel or aluminum build, lift range, saddle design and weight, for SUVs, trucks and household garages.
expertTake: The BIG RED 3 ton service jack with an extra saddle is the best 3 ton floor jack here: a 5-7/8 inch minimum, a 20-7/8 inch maximum and four casters that make it easy to position under an SUV or pickup. The ARCAN A20003 steel jack is the value pick. Skip the aluminum racing jacks if the jack never leaves the garage, because steel is cheaper and tougher.
introParagraphs: A three ton floor jack is the common all-rounder. It has enough rating to lift one end of a mid-size SUV or a half-ton pickup with a margin, and it is still small enough for a home garage. Most households that own one jack own this size.

Within that size, designs vary a lot: steel or aluminum, long or short reach, wide or narrow saddles. This guide compares five jacks of this class on build, lift range, saddle and weight, and explains what each choice means for the car you own.

products.name: BIG RED 3 Ton Hydraulic Trolley Service Floor Jack with Extra Saddle
products.description:
The BIG RED trolley jack is built for SUVs and extended-height trucks. It lifts from 5-7/8 inches to 20-7/8 inches with a 3 ton, 6,000 lb rating, and it comes with an extra long saddle that spreads the load on a frame rail. Two large steel casters and two 360 degree swivel casters make it easy to move and position.

The 5-7/8 inch minimum height is higher than the low profile jacks, so it will not fit under sports cars, and it is a heavy steel tool. Compared with the aluminum VEVOR, it weighs more but is more durable. For an SUV or pickup it is the one to buy.

Ownership is the usual hydraulic care: oil, ram wipe, store lowered. The extra saddle is a practical bonus for frame lifts, and a long-established brand means parts and oil are easy to source. It is a jack you buy once. The extra saddle lives on the handle holder so it does not get lost, and a few drops of oil on the pivots once a year keep the steel casters rolling.
products.bestFor: SUV and pickup owners who want a durable, high-reach jack.
pros: Reaches 20-7/8 in for tall trucks
Extra long saddle spreads the load
Four casters make positioning easy
Established brand with easy parts access
cons: 5-7/8 in minimum will not fit low cars

products.name: LARBANKE 3 Ton Hydraulic Floor Jack, 5.31 to 18.11 in, Carbon Steel
products.description:
The LARBANKE lists a 4.65 inch diameter saddle, wide for this class, which spreads the load on a jack point and reduces slipping. It is made from high-strength carbon steel and lifts 6,600 lb with a 5.31 inch minimum and 18.11 inch maximum, a range that fits most cars, crossovers and SUVs. A lesser known brand is the trade for a lower price tier.

The 18.11 inch maximum falls short of the BIG RED's 20-7/8 inches for tall trucks, and parts support is less proven. Against the ARCAN A20003, it has a larger saddle and a higher rating of 6,600 lb against 6,000 lb. It is a sensible value pick for a household with a car and a crossover.

Keep the oil topped up, wipe the ram and store it lowered. Check the saddle for wear, and use a rubber pad on pinch welds. A thin rubber pad over the saddle protects the paint on a unibody pinch weld, and it costs very little compared with the damage it prevents.
products.bestFor: Cars and crossovers where a wide saddle gives more confidence.
pros: 4.65 in saddle spreads the load
6,600 lb rating on carbon steel
5.31 in to 18.11 in covers most vehicles
Lower price tier than BIG RED
cons: 18.11 in maximum is short for tall trucks

products.name: ARCAN A20003 3 Ton Steel Low Profile Floor Jack
products.description:
The ARCAN A20003 is a steel low profile jack rated for 3 ton, 6,000 lb, for automotive repair, tire service and maintenance. High carbon steel side plates reinforce the chassis for demanding service conditions, and the low profile frame makes it easier to position under cars with low ground clearance.

The listing does not give a height range, so check the minimum and maximum before buying. It is a plain steel jack from a brand known in the trade. Against the aluminum ARCAN A20019 it weighs more but costs less, and against the BIG RED it has a lower profile but less published reach.

Expect typical care: wipe the ram, check the oil and store it lowered. It is a workhorse jack for a household garage and a good choice if you want steel strength at a moderate price. Check the oil level with the ram fully retracted and the jack level, since a tilted jack gives a false reading and leads to overfilling.
products.bestFor: Garage owners who want a straightforward steel 3 ton jack.
pros: High carbon steel side plates add strength
Low profile frame fits many cars
6,000 lb rating for SUVs and cars
Established trade brand
cons: Listing does not state a lift range

products.name: VEVOR 3 Ton Low Profile Aluminum and Steel Racing Floor Jack, 3-6/11 to 19-11/16 in
products.description:
The VEVOR racing jack combines an aluminum body with steel parts, giving a 3 ton, 6,600 lb rating, a 3-6/11 inch minimum and a 19-11/16 inch maximum. That range covers lowered cars and SUVs, which is unusual for a single jack. The mixed construction is lighter than all-steel jacks, which helps if you move it often.

Aluminum dents more easily than steel, and the VEVOR brand is better known for value than for service networks. Compared with the BIG RED it is lighter and lower, but less proven. If you want one jack that fits a sports car and an SUV and can be carried, this is it.

Check the oil, wipe the ram and store it lowered. Keep aluminum parts away from road salt, and inspect the saddle for wear. It is a practical choice for a mixed garage. If you keep it in a trunk, wrap the saddle in a rag so road salt and grit stay off the ram, and rinse the aluminum with fresh water after winter driving.
products.bestFor: Garages with both low cars and SUVs that need a lighter jack.
pros: 3-6/11 in to 19-11/16 in range covers many vehicles
Aluminum and steel build is lighter than all-steel
6,600 lb rating for SUVs
Lower price tier than SATA aluminum
cons: Racing design is less rugged than steel

products.name: ARCAN A20019 3 Ton Aluminum Low Profile Floor Jack, 3.75 to 18 in
products.description:
The ARCAN A20019 is an aluminum 3 ton jack with a 3.75 inch minimum and an 18 inch maximum, rated 6,000 lb for passenger vehicles, SUVs and light trucks. A quick-rise pump brings the saddle to the load fast and reduces effort. It is made by a trade-oriented brand, which makes parts and service easier than for an anonymous import.

Aluminum costs more than steel at this size, and it dents more easily. Compared with the steel ARCAN A20003 it is lighter, and compared with the VEVOR racing jack it has a slightly smaller range but a more established name. It is the premium pick.

Care is simple: keep the ram clean, top up the oil and store it lowered. Aluminum resists rust, which helps in a damp garage or a truck bed. It is a good jack for a shop that moves the jack between bays. Keep it dry between jobs, because even aluminum gets pitted by a damp, salty shed, and a pitted ram chews seals.
products.bestFor: Shops and garages that move the jack around and want a trade brand.
pros: Aluminum body is far lighter than steel
3.75 in to 18 in range covers most vehicles
Quick-rise pump saves effort
Trade brand with easier parts access
cons: Slightly shorter reach than the BIG RED

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 3 ton rating is a lift capacity of 6,000 to 6,600 lb, not the weight of the vehicle. Compare the BIG RED at 6,000 lb with the LARBANKE at 6,600 lb. Because a jack lifts one end or corner, 3 ton is ample for most SUVs and half-ton pickups. The rating assumes a hard level surface and full extension. Never exceed it, and always add jack stands. For a half-ton pickup the front axle often carries more than half the weight, so check the manual before choosing where to lift.

Steel jacks like the BIG RED, LARBANKE and ARCAN A20003 are heavy but tough and cheap. Aluminum jacks like the ARCAN A20019 and the VEVOR racing jack are lighter and resist rust, but dent more easily and cost more. If the jack stays in the garage, steel is the better value. If you carry it, aluminum is worth the premium. A quick way to decide is how many times a year the jack moves out of the garage.

The BIG RED lists 5-7/8 to 20-7/8 inches, the LARBANKE 5.31 to 18.11 inches, the ARCAN A20019 3.75 to 18 inches and the VEVOR 3-6/11 to 19-11/16 inches. A taller truck needs the higher maximum, and a lower car needs the smaller minimum. Measure your jacking points and compare them to these numbers. Bring a tape measure to the car and write down both numbers, because listings round heights.

The LARBANKE lists a 4.65 inch saddle and the BIG RED includes an extra long saddle for frame lifts. A wider saddle spreads the load and reduces slipping. Rubber pads protect pinch welds on unibody cars. If you lift trucks, a large saddle is a safety feature. A tiny steel saddle on a lift point is how jacks slip. Wipe a rubber pad with a damp cloth before use so grit does not scratch the pinch weld.

The BIG RED uses two steel casters and two 360 degree swivel casters, which makes positioning easy. A jack that will not roll straight is annoying and hard to place under a bumper. Check the caster size and swivel design, and favor large rear wheels on rough concrete. Test the roll on your own floor, since a gritty slab binds small casters.

A 3 ton jack carries a vehicle's weight over your head, so brand matters. Trade names like BIG RED and ARCAN are easier to service and find parts for than anonymous imports. Overload valves and published margins help. Whatever you buy, use rated jack stands and never get under a car held only by a jack. Buy the best brand you can afford, because the jack is the one tool that must never fail.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lift range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared minimum and maximum heights. The BIG RED reaches 20-7/8 inches, and the ARCAN A20019 starts at 3.75. Range was matched to the vehicles each jack suits. Taller reach was rewarded only if the jack also fit the stated vehicles.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build material
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared steel and aluminum designs. The BIG RED, LARBANKE and ARCAN A20003 are steel, and the ARCAN A20019 and VEVOR use aluminum. Durability and weight were weighed against price. Durability was weighed against how often the jack moves.

howWeEvaluated.title: Saddle and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at saddle width, extra saddles and casters. The LARBANKE lists a 4.65 inch saddle, and the BIG RED adds an extra long one. Stability under load decided close calls. A bigger pad earned credit on slick surfaces.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and margin
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared ratings. The LARBANKE and VEVOR list 6,600 lb, and the BIG RED and ARCAN list 6,000 lb. We favored jacks with a clear capacity statement. Clear numbers earned credit over vague claims.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brand support and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched price tier to brand strength. BIG RED and ARCAN are trade brands, and the LARBANKE and VEVOR are value imports. Parts access was part of every verdict. A jack that is easy to service is easier to keep.

cards.label: Steel
cards.text: The BIG RED, LARBANKE and ARCAN A20003 are steel. They are tough and cheaper per ton, and they suit a garage jack that rarely moves.

cards.label: Aluminum
cards.text: The ARCAN A20019 and VEVOR use aluminum. They are lighter and rust-resistant, which suits a jack you carry, but they dent more easily.

howToChoose.note: Choose steel for a garage, and aluminum for a jack you carry to a track or a friend's driveway.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A maximum height of at least 18 inches, a wide saddle for the frame or pinch weld and a rating of 6,000 lb or more. Casters matter because SUV jack points are far from the bumper.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The BIG RED 3 Ton fits best with its 20-7/8 inch maximum and extra saddle. The LARBANKE is the lower-cost alternative with a wide saddle.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You lift trucks or want a jack to last decades. The BIG RED and ARCAN A20019 justify the cost with brand support and design.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You jack a car twice a year. The LARBANKE or VEVOR does the job without a premium.

maintenance.why: Low oil makes the lift soft. Use jack oil with the ram retracted. Mark the oil level on a piece of tape for next time.
Grit scores the seals. Wipe it clean and store it lowered. Do this before the ram dries so grit does not set.
Air makes lifts soft. Open the release valve and pump the handle. Repeat three or four cycles with the release valve open.
Dry casters bind and make positioning hard. A drop of light oil on the axle pins is enough.
A cracked weld or worn saddle means it is time to stop using the jack. Replace the jack if you find a crack, not just a worn pad.

faq.q: Is a 3 ton jack enough for an SUV?
faq.a: Yes. A 3 ton jack lifts one end or corner, and an SUV's front end weighs less than 3 tons. Pick a jack with enough reach, like the BIG RED at 20-7/8 inches, and use jack stands.

faq.q: What is the difference between 6,000 and 6,600 lb 3 ton jacks?
faq.a: Makers round differently. A 6,000 lb rating is a true 3 ton, while 6,600 lb uses 2,200 lb per metric ton. Either is fine for most vehicles, but check the stated rating.

faq.q: Is an aluminum floor jack as strong as steel?
faq.a: At the same rating, yes, but aluminum dents more easily and costs more. It is lighter and rust-resistant, which helps if you move the jack.

faq.q: Can I use a 3 ton jack on a truck?
faq.a: For a half-ton pickup, yes, if the maximum height reaches the frame. The BIG RED reaches 20-7/8 inches. Heavier trucks need a 4 ton jack and stands.

faq.q: Do I still need jack stands?
faq.a: Yes. A floor jack lifts, and stands hold the load. Never get under a car supported only by a jack.

faq.q: How do I store a floor jack?
faq.a: Lower the ram fully, wipe it clean and store the jack upright. Keep it dry, and check the oil each season.
